subject: general
question: Which community has the Adi Granth as their Holy Book?
solution:
The correct answer is **Sikhs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Adi Granth, also known as the Guru Granth Sahib, is the central religious scripture of Sikhism.
 
• It was compiled by Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru, in 1604.
 
• The Adi Granth is written in Gurmukhi script and includes hymns from Sikh Gurus and various other saints.
 
• It serves as a guide for Sikhs in their spiritual and daily lives.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1: Buddhists
 Buddhists regard the Tripitaka or Pali Canon as their holy texts.
 
 

 Option 2: Jains
 Jains follow the Agamas and Siddhanta texts as their holy scriptures.
 
 

 Option 3: Jews
 Jews consider the Torah, which is part of the Tanakh, as their sacred scripture.
